Pen Patat

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 1 hr

Pen Patat is a traditional Haitian sweet potato pudding often served during the Fête de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa. This dish honors Papa Zaka, the spirit of agriculture and harvest, by celebrating the bounty of the earth with a rich, comforting dessert made from sweet potatoes and spices.

Ingredients

  • 2 lbs (900 g) sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
  • 1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) evaporated milk
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) coconut milk
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 2 tablespoons (30 g) unsalted butter, melted
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) shredded coconut (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. Boil the sweet potatoes in a large pot of water until tender, about 20 minutes; drain and mash until smooth.
  3. In a large bowl, combine the mashed sweet potatoes, sugar, evaporated milk, coconut milk, eggs, vanilla extract, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and melted butter; mix thoroughly.
  4. Fold in the shredded coconut if using, for added texture and flavor.
  5. Pour the mixture into a greased 8x8-inch (20x20 cm) baking dish and smooth the top.
  6. Bake in the preheated oven for about 45 minutes, or until the pudding is set and the top is lightly browned.
  7. Remove from the oven and let cool slightly before serving.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, substitute half of the evaporated milk with heavy cream.
  • Add a splash of rum or a handful of raisins for a festive twist.
  • Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally topped with a dollop of whipped cream.
